page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an arm64 architecture utilizing the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. The instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage and does not include any GPUs. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the r8gb.12xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in memory operations and multi-threaded processing. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 434.99 GB/sec, and write bandwidth reaches 216.28 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tests also rank in the top 10%, with scores of 524.58 GB/sec and 23,666.0 respectively. Database operations under Passmark score 47,920.83, and static web serving throughput reaches 99.24 GB/sec, both representing top-tier results. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and gzip compression single-threaded benchmarks falling in the middle 50% average tier.

The hardware profile presents specific architectural tradeoffs. While the ARMv9 architecture supports AES cryptography, it lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX. The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage options, though this is mitigated by the 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-core ratio and dedicated physical cores deliver high resource density for memory-bound workloads without hyperthreading overhead. The instance is suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, multi-threaded data processing, and static web serving.
